record.paper_title: Extra extension properties of equidimensional holomorphic mappings: results and open questions
record.context_brief: All-dimensional analogue of the affine-covering corollary
record.original_question: Prove an all-dimensional analogue of Corollary 3.2. In dimension 3, Corollary 3.2 says that if V is a compact affine 3-fold and its universal covering, viewed as a domain over C^3 with locally biholomorphic projection, is pseudoconcave at some boundary point, then V contains a spherical shell of dimension 3. The question asks for the corresponding statement in all dimensions.

evidence.quote: Corollary 3.2 Let V be a compact affine 3-fold and let (Ṽ , π) be its universal covering considered as a domain over C3 with locally biholomorphic projection π. Then if (Ṽ , π) is pseudoconcave at some boundary point then V contains a spherical shell (of dimension 3).
Question 3.3 An analog of Corollary 3.2. in all dimensions seems to be an easier problem then the Question 3.1 in its whole generality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. A compact complex manifold $V$ of complex dimension $n$ is called a compact affine $n$-fold if it admits a holomorphic atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of complex affine maps of $\mathbb{C}^n$; equivalently, the developing map of its universal cover $\tilde V$ is a locally biholomorphic map $\pi : \tilde V \to \mathbb{C}^n$, so that $(\tilde V, \pi)$ is a (Riemann) domain over $\mathbb{C}^n$. Such a domain $(\tilde V, \pi)$ is said to be pseudoconcave at a boundary point $p \in \partial \tilde V$ if there exist a neighborhood basis of $p$ in the relative completion of $\tilde V$ and a $C^2$ defining function whose Levi form has at least one negative eigenvalue at $p$ (equivalently, $\tilde V$ fails to be locally Stein at $p$ from the inside in the strong Levi sense). A spherical shell of dimension $n$ in $V$ is the image, under a holomorphic embedding into $V$, of a domain of the form $\{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : 1 - \varepsilon < \|z\| < 1 + \varepsilon\}$ for some $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, such that this embedded shell is not homologous to zero in $V$ (i.e., a Hartogs-type spherical shell).

Prove or disprove: for every $n \geq 2$, if $V$ is a compact affine $n$-fold whose universal cover $(\tilde V, \pi)$, regarded as a Riemann domain over $\mathbb{C}^n$ with locally biholomorphic projection $\pi$, is pseudoconcave at some boundary point, then $V$ contains a spherical shell of dimension $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for follow-up work generalizing the three-dimensional affine pseudoconcavity / spherical shell statement to all dimensions did not return any paper that explicitly proves or refutes the all-dimensional analogue. No definitive evidence was found that the question has been settled.

status_evidence.title: Affine Manifolds and the Universal Cover
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on affine manifolds and universal covers; no resolution of the all-dimensional pseudoconcavity/spherical-shell question.
status_evidence.claim: No direct resolution of the all-dimensional analogue is found in mainstream affine-manifold references.

status_evidence.title: The universal cover of an affine three-manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Work on universal covers of affine three-manifolds, unrelated to a higher-dimensional generalization of the pseudoconcavity-implies-spherical-shell result.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature on affine universal covers does not address the higher-dimensional analogue.
